taxonomy.source: Kew Plants of the World Online

project_inclusion.native_status_note: Kew currently treats the species as native to Mexico and introduced in Texas. For this project phase, that does not exclude it because the current goal is to study locally encountered Ipomoea and look-alikes.
project_inclusion.local_occurrence_note: Included because it is a locally relevant field species/look-alike in Central Texas and has been encountered/reviewed in the user's recent identification work. Exact target-county native-status auditing is deferred.

morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Blades broadly ovate to nearly orbicular or 3–5-lobed, 50–120 mm long and wide, base cordate, surfaces hairy. Leaf shape is variable and should not be used alone.
morphology_keys.sepals: Five sepals, about 12–24 mm long; proximally broader/ovate, then abruptly narrowing into a long curved or spreading distal tip. At least the proximal portion is hirsute to hispid.
morphology_keys.corolla: Light blue, funnel-shaped, usually about 20–37 mm long (sometimes to ~45 mm), with a white to pale-yellow inner tube.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule; seed characters may be useful in difficult identifications.
morphology_keys.flowering: May–November in Flora of North America treatment.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: Look at the sepals. The long, narrow, curved or spreading distal sepal tips are far more reliable than leaf shape.
fastest_traits: Sepals with strikingly long narrow tips

look_alikes.distinction: I. triloba usually has much shorter sepals (about 5–8 mm) and much smaller corollas, typically under about 2.5 cm. I. hederacea has 12–24 mm sepals with long narrow tips.

Very similar. A New World Ipomoea monograph separates I. hederacea by its generally smaller corolla (<3.5 cm in that key), shorter sepals (<2 cm at anthesis) with recurving tips, and very short peduncle; I. nil has larger flowers and longer sepals.
I. cordatotriloba has shorter, broader sepals without the exaggerated long narrow distal sepal tips typical of I. hederacea.

ecology.habitat: Disturbed sites, roadsides, gravel bars, abandoned plantings and similar open ground.
ecology.regional_status_note: Currently treated as introduced in Texas by Kew.
ecology.study_value: High-value comparison species because leaf shape overlaps with several other Ipomoea; sepal morphology forces attention to stronger diagnostic characters.
